nodes.description: Calcineurin is held inactive by its auto-inhibitory domain, which occupies the catalytic site until calcium/calmodulin binding to the regulatory domain displaces it. Missense variants in the auto-inhibitory domain increase the calmodulin-dependent phosphatase activity of the alpha catalytic subunit. Removing the auto-inhibitory domain altogether, as the truncating p.Gln442Ter variant does, makes the recombinant enzyme almost as active without calmodulin as with it. This is the reverse of DEE91, where catalytic-domain variants reduce activity.
